correctness.rationale: The source central-path identities imply D1=mu diag(x_J^-2), D2^-1=mu diag(s_N^-2). The source resolvent formula gives G=C(C+mu*hhat*I)^-1 with fixed range ran(A_J), so G is I+O(mu) on that range and zero on its orthogonal complement. The block expansion of Y is [[I+O(mu),O(mu^2)],[O(mu),mu Q_perp/h0+o(mu)]]. Q_perp is positive definite because A has full row rank and s_N*>0. Near-identity block Gaussian elimination proves that its m-r small singular values divided by mu converge to eigenvalues of Q_perp/h0; in full-rank support Y tends to I. The 2x3 integer LP exactly satisfies all feasibility, basis, central-path, and partition conditions and yields a diagonal Y with limit gamma1/2. This is a complete analytic proof, with exact fractional finite replay as a secondary check.

originality.rationale: The 2024/2025 quantum-interior-point anchor supplies an O(1/mu) upper bound for its prescribed fixed scalar reduced preconditioner, but neither a rank-sensitive limit nor a sharp exact-central-path witness. Chai--Toh 2007 supplies a broader framework and spectral clustering for different scalar or diagonal proxies, not the exact limiting coefficient of the fixed proxy used in the quantum method. Nine actual semantic searches and targeted primary-literature comparisons found no dominating implication-equivalent theorem. The mathematical contribution is the asymptotic rank dichotomy and coefficient, not the known generic fact that degenerate LP systems can be poorly conditioned.
residual_risks: Earlier spectral preconditioning work may contain an equivalent rank-asymptotic result in different notation despite the examined Chai--Toh propositions.
The exact coefficient applies only when a strictly complementary limit exists, not necessarily to all infeasible-IPM trajectories.
The finding is about condition numbers, not a lower bound on algorithmic quantum query or wall-clock complexity.

value.rationale: The original quantum algorithm explicitly emphasizes reducing ill-conditioning from quadratic to linear reciprocal duality gap but leaves open when that linear dependence is necessary. The theorem gives a natural support-rank criterion: nondegenerate positive support makes its own reduced matrix asymptotically perfectly conditioned, whereas rank-deficient support forces exactly linear blow-up with an explicit coefficient. A minimal integer LP demonstrates that the O(1/mu) rate is sharp even with oracle-perfect partition and exact centrality; this pinpoints which geometric degeneracies require a different preconditioning design. It is a motivated structural boundary, not a generic observation that LPs can be ill-conditioned.
